definitions.explanation: The medically induced loss of sensation or consciousness, used during surgery or dental procedures.

examples.japanese: {麻酔|ますい}が{効|き}いてきた。
{手術|しゅじゅつ}の{前|まえ}に{全身|ぜんしん}{麻酔|ますい}をかけた。
examples.english: General anesthesia was administered before the surgery.

examples.japanese: {歯医者|はいしゃ}で{局所|きょくしょ}{麻酔|ますい}を{打|う}ってもらったが、まだ{少|すこ}し{痛|いた}かった。
examples.english: I had local anesthesia at the dentist, but it still hurt a little.

notes:
USAGE:
Common verbs: {麻酔|ますい}をかける (to administer anesthesia), {麻酔|ますい}が{効|き}く (for anesthesia to take effect), {麻酔|ますい}が{切|き}れる (for anesthesia to wear off).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {全身|ぜんしん}{麻酔|ますい}: general anesthesia
- {局所|きょくしょ}{麻酔|ますい}: local anesthesia
- {麻酔|ますい}をかける: to administer anesthesia
- {麻酔|ますい}が{効|き}く: anesthesia takes effect
- {麻酔|ますい}が{切|き}れる: anesthesia wears off
- {麻酔科医|ますいかい}: anesthesiologist
